ov: Earthworms are soil-dwelling annelids, among nature’s most important recyclers of dead plant matter. They have no skeleton and breathe through their moist skin. Their burrowing mixes and airs the soil, and rich farmland can hold millions of them per hectare.
len: 10 mm to 3 m; the common earthworm about 36 cm
df: Dead plant matter and other organic material in the soil.
fx: Earthworms are food for many animals, from moles and blackbirds to wild boar.
Adult earthworms can regrow lost segments, though how much varies between species.
